extracted.intended_audience: SBIR/STTR applicants and diagnostic assay developers (commercialization, regulatory, manufacturing teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Commercialization and regulatory development plan for a point-of-care lateral flow diagnostic (Active Melioidosis Detect™) submitted as part of an SBIR/STTR application, including product specifications, performance targets, manufacturing and FDA submission strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended Use: In vitro diagnosis of active melioidosis for visual and rapid qualitative detection of the Burkholderia pseudomallei capsular polysaccharide (CPS) antigen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assay intended for diagnosis of B. pseudomallei infection from multiple clinical matrices and for use by trained healthcare professionals; positive AMD results may be confirmed by blood culture (gold standard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Device format and instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Device: Active Melioidosis Detect™ (AMD; Lateral flow immunoassay (LFI)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional instrumentation required; designed for point-of-care and resource-poor settings; buffer/chase buffer should not require cold storage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted sample matrices / analyte
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyte: Whole blood (venous and/or capillary blood), blood, urine, pus, and respiratory secretions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assay also applicable to cultured clinical samples (hemoculture broth, bacterial colonies) and animal samples; intended to detect CPS shed into these matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical sensitivity targets (by matrix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical Sensitivity Pus > 98%; Sputum > 98%; Urine > 95%; Blood > 90%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the performance input targets that the development and validation plan should meet or exceed to support product selection and regulatory submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical specificity target
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical Specificity: ≥95%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical evaluation studies should demonstrate specificity at or above this threshold versus relevant clinical and commensal organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical sensitivity (limit of detection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical sensitivity: Limit of detection ≤ 1 ng/ml CPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical LOD studies should document reproducible detection at or below this CPS concentration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical specificity and cross-reactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical Specificity: Reactivity with B. pseudomallei and B. mallei strains but not other Burkholderia spp.; Cross Reactivity: No reactivity with other pathogenic bacteria e.g. Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reactivity panels should include related Burkholderia species and common pathogenic bacteria to demonstrate specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative / reference methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative Methods: PCR, Immunofluorescence, Culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical/analytical performance should be compared to appropriate reference methods (culture as gold standard; molecular/IFA where relevant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample preparation and time-to-result
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample preparation time: None (depending on the matrix to be used). Reading time (time to result): 5 to 20 minutes (TBD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and validation should demonstrate minimal or no sample prep for intended matrices and consistent reading times facilitating POC use; elsewhere text states 'reduce the time to diagnosis to 10-15 minutes from clinical specimens.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample throughput and usability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample throughput rate: Unlimited. Many samples can be run in parallel on separate strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assay should allow parallel testing and present clear, unambiguous test and control lines for easy interpretation at POC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shelf life and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Shelf life: 24 months at room temperature (≤30°C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability studies should support claimed shelf life at specified temperatures (accelerated and real-time stability testing).

rubrics_metrics.name: General assay characteristics / POC suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The LFI is ideal for the point-of-care and resource poor setting (rapid, sensitive, specific, easy to use, adaptable, allows for random access and cost effective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product design and validations should emphasize simplicity, low-cost reagents, no cold chain for buffer, and minimal training for intended users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagents and detection chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Antibodies to be used: Proprietary antibodies to the B. pseudomallei CPS. Detection agent: Selected antibody(s) to CPS conjugated with gold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conjugate chemistry and antibody selection must be characterized (specificity, affinity) and manufacturing processes for conjugates validated for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance evidence and data supporting candidate selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Data that support the selection of the candidate product for further development: InMAD identified CPS as secreted antigen; qCPS ELISA and AMD LFI identified CPS in filtered urine and serum from patients; preliminary studies show CPS is conserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide reproducible analytical and clinical data (animal and human samples, archived specimens) demonstrating presence/detectability of target antigen to justify development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field study / clinical evaluation design requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To conduct an appropriate, statistically valid evaluation of our tests, it is necessary to perform the field studies with a significant number of samples (good sample size with enough power for significance calculation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field studies should be performed in endemic regions (or with archived positive samples), be statistically powered, and capture relevant matrices and clinical conditions; use of data-capture tools (e.g., Deki reader, cloud capabilities) recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field testing protocol for external participating labs (DMAWG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work plan for participating sites: perform blood culture, Gram stain and oxidase tests; use AMD LFI on Gram-negative oxidase-positive bacilli; further evaluate positives per SOPs; CDC may offer confirmation; ethical clearance if required; report aggregated results (how many used, how many positive, final identification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide SOPs, reporting templates, and channels for confirmation and expert advice; emphasize aggregated result reporting and options for collaborative case reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory submission timeline and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal is submission of a 510(k) application (by the end of Project Year 3) and FDA clearance; draft pre-submission to FDA in Project Year 2 to seek advice and requirements for prospective studies and review of in-house performance studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan presubmission meetings, define prospective clinical study requirements, and align analytical/clinical package to FDA expectations to support 510(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory & quality support activities (services)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory items to be covered: Development of pre-market submission strategies; Premarket submission preparation (510(k)s, PMAs, IDEs, reclassification petitions, etc.) and reviews; FDA correspondence; Procedure and user manual development; Assistance with FDA compliance matters, GMP/QSR reviews, development and auditing (including SOP development and review); Good clinical practice auditing; Clinical protocol development; Statistical support services; FDA staff meeting preparation and participation; FDA Advisory Panel preparation and participation; Technology and regulatory due diligence assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure availability of experienced regulatory and clinical support (in-house or consultants) to execute these activities as part of the product development plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: GLP / GMP compliance and phased manufacturing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with GLP defined by 21 CFR (58) and cGMP defined by 21 CFR (211): Prototype LFIs will be produced under GLP (Project Years 1-2) and the optimized LFI will be produced under GMP (Project Years 2-3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign oversight for GLP/GMP compliance (qualified RA personnel), ensure training, and transition documentation/processes from GLP to GMP as development progresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design controls and design history file (DHF)
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by CFR 820.30, The Contractor shall maintain a design history file that contains or references the design of this assay. It will include the design plan, design specifications, protocols for the studies to be conducted, study results and associated data, a record of project meeting minutes and design review minutes, and copies of all communications with collaborators and FDA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and maintain a design plan and DHF from project inception; schedule formal design reviews and document inputs/outputs as required by design control regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design review body and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning of this project, InBios shall establish a design review body consisting of scientists, clinicians, and experts in regulatory affairs, quality control and manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design review body should meet regularly, assess developmental work, document discussions, and recommend future efforts; all inputs and design outputs must be traceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing process control and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: All critical processes are validated to ensure consistency and compliance with design specifications. All operators are trained to carry out and document procedures. Deviations are investigated and documented. Records of manufactured goods that enable the complete history of a batch to be traced are retained in a comprehensible and accessible form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement process validation, operator training programs, deviation handling procedures, and batch record retention to support GMP compliance and traceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality systems and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: InBios is FDA registered and an ISO (International Organization for Standardization) certified company; InBios became ISO 13485:2003 certified in 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain appropriate quality system registration/certification (FDA establishment registration, ISO 13485) and adhere to QSR/Design Controls across development and manufacturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical and laboratory study requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory studies: accelerated stability, cross reactivity, interference and precision; Analytical sensitivity and specificity studies; Prototype and beta test development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct and document a full suite of analytical studies (stability, interference, cross-reactivity, precision/reproducibility) to support performance claims and regulatory submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial and study management
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical trial management; clinical protocol development; good clinical practice auditing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan statistically powered clinical studies, engage biostatistical support, and apply GCP auditing to clinical sites and data collection for regulatory acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and biostatistics support
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that a consultant will perform Biostatistics. Statistical support services listed under regulatory items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include biostatistical expertise for study design, sample size/power calculations, analysis plans, and FDA submission statistical sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of field initiative results and data sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: For DMAWG field initiative: overall results to receive back are i) how many tests were used?, ii) how many were positive? and iii) what is the final identification of those positive isolates? The DMAWG will release the results only as an overall result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate reporting from participating sites is required; individual site case reports possible with collaboration; ensure compliance with local ethics/EC requirements if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics / local approvals for field work
rubrics_metrics.description: There is usually no need for Ethical Clearance for work of this nature. However, if the participating site considers that it is required, it is the responsibility of the participating site to obtain EC clearance prior to participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify local regulatory/ethics requirements before initiating field studies; document any required approvals in study records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market, customer and competitive positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Market, Customer, and Competition: anticipate AMD marketing analogous to FDA cleared Kalazar Detect™ test; niche focus on emerging/international infectious diseases and biodefense; customers include clinicians in endemic regions and potential end users in DHS/DoD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization planning should demonstrate market need, potential end-users, competitive analysis, and go-to-market strategy including export/FDA/CE considerations.
